correctness.rationale: Continuous spectral functional calculus yields ||Re(e^{-it}U)||=cos distance to antipodal spectrum; complement arcs have nearest-endpoint distance min(x,ell-x). Integrating gives (ell-sin ell)/2 per gap; countable additivity is valid because the sum of gap lengths is at most pi. Strict sine concavity and strict increase of q sin(pi/q) prove both equality classifications and the sharp n-dimensional bound. Scalar and dense/projective-full boundary cases have been checked analytically; numerical tests are auxiliary.

This result computes it for every unitary from intrinsic spectral gap geometry and determines the exact and strictly dimension-dependent optimum plus all eigenvalue patterns attaining it. Both the infinite-spectrum identity and the finite-dimensional classification are natural spectral-operator invariants, not arbitrary parameter slices; the structural answer guides the geometry of extremizing unitary spectra.
